debate.situation: You are the one who arranges the meetups with a friend. The time together is lovely, but when you stop texting, the contact stops, and you wonder whether to say something. You have reported the pattern. You have not reported why it happens, whether your friend would notice if told, or what you hope would change. That gap is decisive, because the same pattern can come from busyness, habit, or lower interest, and each calls for a different move.

minds.title: The Candid Friend
minds.concern: Sincerity: a friendship should be able to hold the truth about how it feels, including the awkward parts.
minds.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

minds.title: The Needs Translator
minds.concern: How to say it: turning a hurt into a clear, non-accusing request so the other person can actually respond.
minds.author: Marshall B. Rosenberg

minds.title: The Maintenance Realist
minds.concern: How friendships actually work: they need regular upkeep, and uneven initiating is common and not always a sign of caring less.
minds.author: Robin Dunbar
minds.book: Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships

debate.speaker: The Candid Friend
debate.text: Yes, say something. Emerson wrote: "A friend is a person with whom I may be sincere." If you can be honest about the lovely evenings but not about this nagging pattern, the friendship is more polite than it looks. Swallowing it is not the kind option.
debate.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
debate.basis: Basis: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series

debate.speaker: The Needs Translator
debate.text: Say something, yes, but mind the shape. Opening with you never reach out is an accusation in a sensible coat. Separate what you noticed from what you feel and what you want, then make one small, specific request. That last part is my own addition, not just the book.
debate.author: Marshall B. Rosenberg
debate.basis: Basis: Marshall B. Rosenberg, Nonviolent Communication

debate.speaker: The Maintenance Realist
debate.text: You are both skipping a step. the research of Dunbar on friendship points to contact as the thing that keeps closeness alive, and someone has to supply it. Some people are wonderful company and poor initiators. That is a habit, not automatically a verdict. Why open with a confrontation?
debate.author: Robin Dunbar
debate.book: Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships
debate.basis: Basis: Robin Dunbar, Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships

debate.speaker: The Candid Friend
debate.text: Because from outside, a habit and a verdict look identical, and calling it logistics can be a way of dodging the talk. The words always the one suggest it already weighs on you. Maybe it is tiredness, maybe a fear of mattering less. Those are different problems.
debate.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
debate.basis: Basis: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series

debate.speaker: The Maintenance Realist
debate.text: Fair, I will narrow my claim: it may be a habit, and I cannot prove it. And I would add a third possibility, that the weight is about being worth effort. The fact that would reorder everything is how your friend reacts when told. Surprise suggests oblivion; a shrug suggests something else.
debate.author: Robin Dunbar
debate.book: Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships
debate.basis: Basis: Robin Dunbar, Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships

debate.speaker: The Needs Translator
debate.text: And the request differs by branch. If it is tiredness, you ask to share the planning. If it is wanting to feel valued, you ask for a sign that she looks forward to seeing you. Same conversation, different ask. Which one you need is yours to rank.
debate.author: Marshall B. Rosenberg
debate.basis: Basis: Marshall B. Rosenberg, Nonviolent Communication

debate.speaker: The Candid Friend
debate.text: Then I object to the obvious alternative of the Realist, going quiet to see what happens. It is a test your friend does not know she is taking, and you would learn only how long silence takes to bother her. That is a stratagem, not sincerity.
debate.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
debate.basis: Basis: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series

debate.speaker: The Maintenance Realist
debate.text: Conceded as a secret test: it is unfair and hard to interpret, since silence has many causes. But waiting has value if narrowed. Let one gap run a little longer than usual, without punishment or scorekeeping, and you gather evidence before deciding whether anything needs saying.
debate.author: Robin Dunbar
debate.book: Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships
debate.basis: Basis: Robin Dunbar, Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships

debate.speaker: The Needs Translator
debate.text: Waiting has a cost, though: resentment builds in the meantime, and then the talk arrives with an edge. Better to speak while the evenings are still lovely. Something like: I enjoy our time, I have noticed I usually set it up, and I would like you to suggest the next one.
debate.author: Marshall B. Rosenberg
debate.basis: Basis: Marshall B. Rosenberg, Nonviolent Communication

debate.speaker: The Candid Friend
debate.text: I accept the gentle wording; you have also kept the honesty, which is my concern. But I hold this: she may hear criticism whatever the phrasing. Her reaction is not a failure of the method. It is information about whether the friendship has room for this kind of talk.
debate.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
debate.basis: Basis: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series

debate.speaker: The Maintenance Realist
debate.text: Agreed, and one outcome deserves a fair hearing: she values you, will happily turn up, and simply never plans. Then the friendship has a different shape, you plan and she shows up. Whether that is acceptable or unequal is a real disagreement, and not mine to settle.
debate.author: Robin Dunbar
debate.book: Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships
debate.basis: Basis: Robin Dunbar, Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships

debate.clearer: The pattern itself is not yet evidence of what your friend feels; it fits busyness, habit, or lower interest equally well. The minds converged on one point: if you speak, a warm, specific request keeps the honesty without turning it into an accusation. They still disagree about whether to wait and watch first, and about whether a friendship where you always plan is acceptable if she clearly values you. One possible self-reflection: is the sting about the effort of planning, or about wanting a sign that you are looked forward to? Those may pull in different directions, and which matters more is for you to rank.
debate.dependsOn:
If the evenings are warm and the effort feels like a small burden you mostly accept, a light, low-stakes mention or simply a shared-planning request becomes more reasonable, because it asks for little and tests whether she responds.
If the pattern leaves you feeling unimportant or resentful, saying something soon becomes more reasonable, because waiting tends to let that feeling harden and colour the talk later.
If you suspect it is mostly habit or a busy period, trying a slightly longer gap first, without any scorekeeping, becomes more reasonable, because it gathers evidence at little cost.
If you do not know how she would respond, the proportionate way to learn is a gentle, specific request and watching whether she follows through over a few weeks, rather than judging by one reaction.
